binding_fences.authority: UK_COVERAGE_PROGRESS.md real-donor HMRC replay (2026-07-13); canonical fences in microcosm.build.uk_runtime.hmrc_replay.
binding_fences.rule: No local target family may bind facts banded by SPI Total Income: the FRS instrument cannot materialize complete Total Income, so band membership is unassignable. This is the census's application of the national adjudication that holds all 208 published banded facts as fenced exclusions (the canonical fence text lives with the national constants); minting banded local variants is forbidden.

binding_fences.authority: uk_population_targets.json declarations hmrc.employment_income.amount, hmrc.employment_income.count, hmrc.self_employment_income.amount, hmrc.self_employment_income.count and hmrc.higher_rate_taxpayers.count (their income_tax_before_winter_fuel_payment_charge_annual filter); microcosm#495 scoping.
binding_fences.rule: The declared HMRC area metrics gate frame membership on modeled income_tax_before_winter_fuel_payment_charge_annual > 0 (each person's income tax over the 12 months before their FRS interview, a proxy for the tax year, before the Winter Fuel Payment charge) — a model-output proxy for 'taxpayer in the SPI frame', not a source-faithful frame. Binding any HMRC area family requires an explicit adjudication accepting or replacing that proxy before targets enter a solve.

binding_fences.authority: ONS income estimates for small areas QMI (FRS-based method); microcosm#495 scoping.
binding_fences.rule: ONS income estimates for small areas are model-based outputs built from the Family Resources Survey. Calibrating FRS-derived microdata to them feeds the instrument back into itself; binding requires an explicit adjudication of that circularity (accept with documented rationale, or reject the family).

binding_fences.authority: ONS income estimates for small areas, England and Wales, financial year ending 2023 (comparability guidance); microcosm#495 scoping (cross-family review finding).
binding_fences.rule: The runtime's ons/equiv_housing_costs metric has no declared supplier: ONS states its small-area BHC and AHC income estimates are independently modelled and should not be directly compared, so their difference is not a publishable housing-costs target. Binding the equivalised-income family must target the published BHC and AHC measures separately or document a different housing-costs source.

binding_fences.authority: DWP Universal Credit official statistics Stat-Xplore user guide (household definition); uk_population_targets.json declarations dwp.uc.households_by_area and dwp.uc.households_by_area_children_{0,1,2,3plus} (benefit-unit bindings mapped to households, which local_targets.compute_household_metrics sums); microcosm#495 scoping (cross-family review finding).
binding_fences.rule: The runtime maps benefit-unit-level UC receipt and each UC benefit unit's uc_calibration_child_count band (the FRS-role UC child count) onto household rows by sum: a physical household containing two UC benefit units contributes 2 to uc_households and one contribution to each unit's child band. This aligns the runtime with DWP UC claim households, which correspond to benefit units rather than physical FRS households; binding must preserve this reviewed grain crosswalk.

binding_fences.authority: ONS/NRS/NISRA statistical disclosure control documentation; microcosm#495 scoping (cross-family review measurement).
binding_fences.rule: All three census household-count legs are disclosure-controlled (ONS/NRS cell-key perturbation; NISRA table-builder controls). Per-area dispersion of the retired OA-ladder sums against the published cells at review: England mean 7.4 / max 29, Wales 6.4 / 15, Scotland net −557 (NRS applies disclosure control per output level; same shortfall at both grains), Northern Ireland mean 7 / max 16 after the NI constituency leg moved to NISRA's published DZ2021→PARLCON24 lookup (the earlier postcode inference was a mapping defect of 10 Data Zones, max 694, not perturbation). When a national same-concept control is bound, the standing cross-grain rule declared in uk_runtime.ledger_targets rescales both grains; country wins. The census cells count the occupied-household universe and pair only through the household-composition bridge, never with dwelling stock; that cross-grain rescale applies once the bridge is bound. Bound from microcosm#791 (2026-09-11): the three ONS household-composition cells that held the bridge reviewed-unbound now bind on the frs_relationships household type, so the cross-grain rescale runs on the A15-uprated cells; the ten-cell partition and the A15 control are both ons.households_total, so the declared factor is 1 by closure and the receipt records the bridge as bound.

binding_fences.authority: FRS background and methodology (private-household universe); ONS population estimates methodology (communal-establishment population); microcosm#495 scoping (cross-family review finding).
binding_fences.rule: The FRS covers private households, while ONS mid-year population estimates cover the total usual-resident population including communal establishments (care homes, student halls, barracks, prisons). Binding age-structure targets must declare the universe treatment (communal-establishment adjustment or documented acceptance) per area type.

binding_fences.authority: uk-data targets/sources/la_council_tax.py lineage doctrine and datasets/local_areas/local_authorities/loss.py; uk-data#371; uk-data#457; microcosm#147 adjudication A3; microcosm#929 basis ruling 2026-09-15.
binding_fences.rule: Council-tax stock targets count dwellings, not households. The family binds the councils' taxbase returns, which count the dwellings charged as a sole or main residence once second homes and empty dwellings are taken out (England, Wales) or the chargeable dwellings (Scotland); the VOA valuation-list stock, which also carries exempt, empty and second-home dwellings, ran 6 % over the household frame and is not bound. The residual between the taxbase universe and occupied private households in the FRS frame needs an explicit adjudication naming it.

binding_fences.authority: HM Land Registry Price Paid Data guidance; UK HPI methodology; ONS NSPL user guide; VOA CTSOP1.1; OBR costing of the high value council tax surcharge (April 2026) paragraph 1.13; PolicyEngine/chronicle#343 boundary ruling; microcosm#1240 plan rulings of 2026-10-13.
binding_fences.rule: The high-value homes family binds a Microcosm-derived estimate of the owner-occupied dwelling stock above value thresholds, not a publisher count. Each assumption needs an in-force adjudication: the latest non-bulk category A sale values each dwelling sold since 1995; the UK HPI by local authority and property type moves it to the calendar-2024 average (region, then nation, as fallbacks; the Isles of Scilly take Cornwall's index); dwellings never sold since 1995 are assumed to share the sold stock's value distribution within a local authority (the private-sector VOA stock over the valued dwellings); the owner-occupied share is the census share of the private stock, rescaled to the OBR costing note's national control on dwellings over 2 million; registrations lag sales by weeks to months; England and Wales only. The coverage correction is the main sensitivity: it lifts the sold stock by a median authority ratio of about 1.5, and with it the England owner-occupied count over 2 million sits about a sixth above the OBR-implied figure (the no-correction and no-control variants are receipted in uk/high_value_home_stock.provenance.json). The English region and Wales rows of the same estimate bind on the local line only, as the cross-grain control for the area cells, so the fence covers them too (microcosm#1301).

binding_fences.authority: DESNZ sub-national electricity and gas consumption statistics methodology notes; DESNZ Energy Trends tables 4.1 and 5.5; microcosm#1207 plan rulings of 2026-10-14 (reconcile onto the stage's level); DESNZ's Northern Ireland sub-national electricity and gas statistics, with the Northern Ireland sentence re-worded in by María on 2026-10-17 (microcosm#1306 review); electricity levelled to ONS 04.5.1 by María's ruling of 2026-10-28 (microcosm#1418).
binding_fences.rule: DESNZ's sub-national consumption is not the level the lcfs stage rakes every household's kWh to (Energy Trends, or for a fuel the stage levels to ONS household spending, the kWh that spending buys at QEP prices): it reads electricity from 31 January to 30 January on non-half-hourly meters and over the calendar year on half-hourly meters (as reported), and gas from mid-May to mid-May (weather-corrected), and its Great Britain totals sit above the stage level's Great Britain part. The family binds DESNZ's split between authorities, not its level: one factor per fuel puts the cells on the stage's level (desnz.energy_trends.gb_domestic_level), and the cells keep the fact's own year (a matched-period hold). Great Britain's part of the stage's UK level is its share of DESNZ's sub-national consumption with Northern Ireland's all-domestic row added, whose electricity runs on financial years and gas on Northern Ireland gas years, figures DESNZ calls not directly comparable with Great Britain's. Binding needs an adjudication that the split is the target and the basis gap is not.

binding_fences.authority: DESNZ sub-national gas consumption statistics methodology (meter classification); microcosm#890 F (the stage's published connection share); microcosm#1207 plan of 2026-10-14.
binding_fences.rule: The gas-connected cells read an area's domestic gas meters over its domestic electricity meters as the share of its households connected to gas. Meters are not households: a dwelling can carry more than one meter, a meter can serve an empty dwelling or a second home, and DESNZ classes a gas meter as domestic by a consumption threshold. The share is applied to the area's census households, whose level the household controls set through the census partition. Binding needs an adjudication accepting the ratio as the household share.

The lcfs stage already imposes the same published ratio by region (gas meters over electricity meters by FRS region), so the authority cells constrain a quantity the stage set: within a region they add the split between authorities, and the region's weighted share follows from them. The kWh cells likewise sit on the level the stage raked to. An adjudication names this overlap.

binding_fences.authority: DESNZ sub-national electricity and gas consumption statistics, and DESNZ LSOA and data zone domestic consumption statistics (December 2025 release, 2024 data); the committed atomic supports (uk/uk_atomic_area_supports.provenance.json); microcosm#1095 plan approved by María on 2026-10-25 (split by DESNZ's small areas, not by households).
binding_fences.rule: DESNZ publishes no constituency cut. The constituency cells are Microcosm's split of each authority's published total over its constituencies, in proportion to DESNZ's own LSOA (England and Wales, 2021) and data zone (Scotland, 2022) figures for the same year and basis. An LSOA or data zone whose output areas fall in two seats is split by their census households, and DESNZ's unallocated meters (about 0.1% of Great Britain) follow the split. Every authority keeps its published total, so the two grains' kWh cells agree within each region and the single-winner rule rescales the authority cells by one. Two steps are modelled, both small: each output area goes to one seat through ONS's best-fit lookup of 2021 output areas to July 2024 constituencies (NRS's lookup of 2022 output areas in Scotland), and use per household is assumed uniform within a small area that straddles two seats (2.4% of households). The gas-connected cells do not agree by construction: each area's are its census households times its own meter share. After the census reconciliation the two grains' sums differ by under 0.2% in every region (0.06% over Great Britain, on the 272c987 feed). Binding needs an adjudication that a seat's split is the target, not a published fact.

acceptance_criteria_to_mechanism.binding_requires_review: require_adjudicated_uk_local_binding refuses a family whose declared fences lack an in-force local_binding_adjudications row.
acceptance_criteria_to_mechanism.every_target_accounted: The local target compiler requires a compiled reference or an AreaSignedDeferral for every metric-by-area cell; unsigned and stale missing-data deferrals raise, while a separately adjudicated compilable deferral requires an explicit opt-in.
acceptance_criteria_to_mechanism.intentional_zeros_preserved: Finite zero facts compile unchanged and are distinguished from missing or unreachable nonzero targets.
acceptance_criteria_to_mechanism.missing_cells_masked_deliberately: AreaSignedDeferral is the deliberate compile-time mask; the solve accepts only finite rows.
acceptance_criteria_to_mechanism.no_silent_target_fabrication: The compiler reads only the sha-pinned Ledger feed, and the devolved_housing population-share allocation is a reviewed non-port.

masked_missing.enforcement_point: Both refusals fire inside the reference compiler, which runs only when the surface is regenerated against the pinned consumer feed (a licensed, untracked input passed explicitly to tools/generate_uk_local_target_references.py). CI verifies the committed compile through the census and membership drift gates; it cannot re-run the compiler, so a feed that later carries new facts is caught at the next regeneration, not continuously.
masked_missing.incumbent_comparison: This supersedes uk-data's per-cell NaN mask with a stronger, reviewable compile-time accounting contract.
masked_missing.rule: A local target excluded at compile time is represented by an AreaSignedDeferral carrying a signed reason and explicit area ids. Unsigned absence raises, and a missing-data deferral becomes stale and raises as soon as the pinned feed can compile that cell. A separate adjudication may defer a compilable lower-grain fact only through the explicit defer_if_compiles opt-in.
masked_missing.solve_semantics: The solve surface remains dense and finite by design; local_rowwise.py refuses non-finite targets rather than treating NaN as an implicit loss mask.

never_fabricate.cautionary_example: uk-data datasets/local_areas/constituencies/devolved_housing.py allocated hardcoded Wales and Scotland rent totals across constituencies in proportion to age-target population. Those anchors are deliberately not ported.
never_fabricate.replacement: Record signed absence, a reviewed exclusion, or a declared cross-grain bridge backed by a pinned crosswalk; never mint cells.
never_fabricate.rule: Never create a local target by allocating a national or country total across areas by population share or another smooth proxy.

zero_targets.enforcement: Zero is preserved as a finite target; only an unreachable nonzero target is refused by the matrix builder.
zero_targets.rule: A published zero-valued local target is legal and intentional.

families.description: SPI-frame employment and self-employment income amounts and taxpayer counts by area.
Household members by ten-year age band.

Weighted household counts by area, compiled from Chronicle's sha-pinned Census 2021 and 2022 household facts. Census occupied households match the FRS household frame, so the person-universe adjudication does not bind here.
Universal Credit benefit units summed onto household rows, and (constituency only) their split by each benefit unit's uc_calibration_child_count (the FRS-role UC child count).
Equivalised household disposable income before/after housing costs and implied housing costs (local-authority metrics).
Private rent paid by privately renting households (local-authority cells, and Scotland's BRMA cells, where PIPR publishes Scottish rents).

Owner-occupied dwellings valued above £1m, £1.5m and £2m (April 2026 prices) by constituency and local authority, England and Wales, from HM Land Registry Price Paid Data uprated with the UK HPI and placed through the NSPL and the committed atomic support (microcosm#1240, fix 2). The counts are Microcosm's computation from raw-only Chronicle registrations, carried in the committed derived-facts resource; the frame measures the stored main_residence_value of owner households at the dataset period against thresholds deflated to the same price basis. The English region and Wales rows of the same estimate (microcosm.high_value_homes.*_by_region) bind on the local line only, as the cross-grain control for these cells, except the North East and Wales rows over £2m, which are signed out below the 400-home floor (microcosm#1301). The family covers owner-occupiers' main residences only: second homes, let property and homes owned by companies or non-residents are outside it until the coverage decision (microcosm#1240 fix 6, tracked on microcosm#1095).

Domestic electricity and gas consumption (kWh) and gas-connected households by local authority, Great Britain, from DESNZ's sub-national statistics (microcosm#1207). The kWh cells keep DESNZ's split between authorities at the lcfs stage's Energy Trends level (one factor per fuel); the gas-connected cells are each authority's census households times its gas meters over its electricity meters, a member of the census household partition. The frame reads each household's stored spend at the dataset period and turns it back into kWh at the stage's declared prices. DESNZ publishes no constituency cut, so the constituency cells bind Microcosm's split of each authority's totals by DESNZ's LSOA and data zone figures, which keeps every authority's total (microcosm#1095).

Dwellings charged council tax by band at local-authority grain, from the councils' taxbase returns (England A-H, Wales A-I, Scotland A-H), represented on the household frame (microcosm#929). The nine composed English region controls sum all 296 authority facts, including the two support-floor-deferred authorities (Isles of Scilly in the South West, City of London in London), so the cross-grain operator rescales those regions' bound cells by the whole-region sum over the bound sum: about a thousand dwellings on the South West's band A, the same shape the VOA basis had. England's authorities also bind line 8, the dwellings with the single adult household 25% discount (microcosm#1095): the cells share the national single adult row's measurement, so the England row is their control.

status_definitions.bound_in_code: The household-side metric is computed today by local_targets.compute_household_metrics from its declaration's policyengine binding in uk_population_targets.json.
status_definitions.documented_unpinned: The official product exists and was verified at the recorded URL on verified_on, but no exact table, vintage, or hash is pinned; binding work pins it per family.
status_definitions.pinned_in_derived_resource: The official product is pinned in Chronicle, registered raw-only (its bytes pinned by sha256 but parsed into no fact) or parsed into the sha-pinned feed, and Microcosm's committed derived-facts resource, built by the recorded tool from those pins, carries the target values; derived_resource_pin records the resource and its row digest.
status_definitions.pinned_in_ledger_facts: The official product's target facts are present in the sha-pinned Ledger consumer fact feed recorded on the source row.
status_definitions.review_required_before_binding: The fence is a reviewed adjudication requirement enforced by the rowwise doctrine solve (local_rowwise.require_adjudicated_uk_local_binding): binding a family whose fences lack an in-force entry in local_binding_adjudications.json is refused before any solve runs.
status_definitions.signed_deferred: The official product is present or documented, but this target surface does not bind it in the current compile; the source row carries signed_reason_id and signed_rationale.
